items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: So, Glenn and I called him from the Roosevelt, and Glenn could only afford $90, you see.

ctx.x: And it was a bad band, and Foss didn't like it, but he was making Arnett the Quarter Week, which was good money in those days. So, Glenn and I called him from the Roosevelt, and Glenn could only afford $90, you see. So he told me, he said, Faz, I can only pay you $90 now, but this is, this band's going to be a good band. So Faz quit. Arnheim had come down here and joined Glenn, and he wanted me to go with him on drums. But I was making more money than that around here, because at the time I was on the staff band…

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: well not only Pollock, but Miller.

ctx.x: Was it good or is it funny?

It was marvelous Bill, but it was the stinkinest tone, it was like Fazola playing the saxophone. Fazola was the world's worst sounding saxophone player that you ever heard in your life. In fact, cause Benny Pollock, two or three times, well not only Pollock, but Miller. And a lot of the band wanted him to play the lead, cause Fazola was a marvelous musician, you know. I mean he read the seven clefs and all. But man, the tone he got out of the saxophone, the sound of Sidney Ironman, the same Rapolo was the same…
But what about Snoozer? You were going to tell about how?
